page: OVHcloud r2-30 is a memory-optimized virtual server instance running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by a dedicated Intel processor based on the Haswell microarchitecture with 2 physical cores and 2 vCPUs running at 2.2 GHz. The system is equipped with 30.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 15.0 GB per core. Local storage consists of a bundled 50 GB SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results indicate that the r2-30 sits in the lower performance tiers. Both single-core and multi-core CPU benchmarks, such as stress-ng and Geekbench, place the instance in the bottom 10% of tested hardware. Memory bandwidth tests show weak to poor performance, with cached small-block reads reaching 175.97 GB/sec and uncached large-block reads and writes falling into the bottom 10% at 7.81 GB/sec and 10.54 GB/sec respectively. Database and caching operations, such as Redis SET, perform in the bottom 25% with 2.93 million operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the r2-30 offers a high memory capacity relative to its compute resources, making it a budget-friendly option for memory-bound workloads that do not require high CPU performance. The trade-off is the older Intel Haswell CPU architecture and lower overall processing throughput. This instance is best suited for workloads such as lightweight database hosting, caching layers, memory-intensive background workers, or basic web serving where memory capacity is prioritized over raw computational speed.
